messages:
sylvia: quick follow-up from the autoscale RFC — we need to pick one approach for lane sizing: per-tenant elastic lanes vs a global prewarm reservoir. pros/cons below, thoughts?

ajay: per-tenant lanes => better isolation & predictable SLOs but multiplies headroom + cost. global pool saves $$ but noisy neighbors.

maria: +1 on isolation for strict SLO customers, but we saw fragmentation spikes in the last replay test. hybrid seems promising: small tenant lanes + shared reservoir for bursts.

nate: agree hybrid. also think the operator should own sizing decisions using local util signals, not the CP. CP should only declare intents.

autoscale-bot: scale-loop: missed-evict=2, metric-gap=KV_CACHE_HIT_RATE undefined at 2025-11-02T14:22:03Z

ajay: proposal: operator-managed bounded lane state machine. semantics: min_shards from committed SLA, target_shards from EWMA(util), burst credits from shared reservoir. CP only sends SLA + credit assignments. operator admits/evicts locally.

sylvia: that cleans the CP surface. keeps math close to runtime and reduces cross-component churn.

maria: testing and observability are big risks. need per-lane telemetry (lane_id, tenant_id, util, headroom_consumed). also token-level cost tagging for regressions.

sylvia: and add a circuit-breaker: if reservoir_level < 20% then start degrading by routing low-priority tenants to model-variant fallback.

ajay: sketched config for prototype:
```
lane_policy:
  min_shards: commit_based
  util_target: 0.65
  ewma_window: 30s
  max_shards: 16
  reservoir_threshold_pct: 20
```

nate: can we include a small "grace_tokens" buffer per-tenant so short hot bursts don't get preempted instantly? credit pool + decay would help UX.

maria: agree, but need strict accounting to prevent freeloaders. grace_tokens should be charged over time and visible in billing logs.

sylvia: decision draft: prototype operator-driven lane-sizing + shared reservoir. CP provides SLA & committed credits, operator emits intents and makes admission/eviction decisions based on local util + reservoir. fallback routing on low reservoir. next steps: spike testbench + telemetry dashboard.

ajay: i'll own the prototype. plan: bench sim to model tenant mixes, k8s operator PoC, then smoke tests. assigning to @ajay :point_right:

maria: i'll own dashboards and SLO checks. will add regression alerts for cost/latency.

sylvia: thanks — i'll write the follow-up RFC with config examples, test plan, and rollout canary plan. :rocket:
